title: Something's wrong--perhaps a missing \item on Mac (move the text out of the list)
short_title: LaTeX says perhaps a missing \item? Check the line above it

runs.cmd: cd "$(mktemp -d)" && print -rl -- '\documentclass{article}' '\begin{document}' '\begin{itemize}' 'Things to pack:' '\item Passport' '\item Charger' '\end{itemize}' '\end{document}' > main.tex && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex > out.txt; grep -m1 '^! LaTeX' out.txt; grep -m1 '^l\.[0-9]' out.txt; sed -n '3,4p' main.tex; grep -c '^!' out.txt
runs.output:
! LaTeX Error: Something's wrong--perhaps a missing \item.
l.5 \item P
\begin{itemize}
Things to pack:
1

runs.cmd: cd "$(mktemp -d)" && print -rl -- '\documentclass{article}' '\begin{document}' 'Things to pack:' '\begin{itemize}' '\item Passport' '\item Charger' '\end{itemize}' '\end{document}' > main.tex && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex > out.txt; sed -n '3,4p' main.tex; grep -c '^!' out.txt

verify.notes: Each run writes a small article in a fresh temporary folder and builds it once with pdfLaTeX from TeX Live 2026 in nonstop mode. With a line of plain text between \begin{itemize} and the first \item, the log holds one error, Something's wrong--perhaps a missing \item, reported at line 5 (the first \item), not at line 4 where the stray text is. With that line moved above \begin{itemize}, the same list builds and the log holds no error lines. The TeX FAQ and the Overleaf error page both give text in a list with no \item in front of it as the plain cause of this message.

scenes.title: Perhaps a missing \item
scenes.sub: Your list has items. Look one line up.
scenes.narration: LaTeX says perhaps a missing item, but your list has items. Look one line above the one it names.

scenes.label: Terminal
lines: ! LaTeX Error: Something's wrong--perhaps a missing \item.
scenes.narration: Here is the error. LaTeX reports it at line five, the first item. But line four, just after begin itemize, is a line of plain text.

scenes.text: Inside a list, every piece of text has to belong to an \item. LaTeX only notices the stray text when it reaches the next \item, so it reports that line instead.
scenes.narration: Inside a list, every piece of text has to belong to an item. A heading or a sentence placed after begin itemize belongs to none. LaTeX only notices when it reaches the next item, so the line number it gives is the item after the stray text.

scenes.label: main.tex
lines: Find the text between \begin{itemize} and the first \item
scenes.narration: Find the text that sits between begin itemize and the first item. Move it above begin itemize, or put backslash item in front of it if it should be an entry. Then build again.

scenes.label: Terminal
scenes.narration: With the text above the list, the same document builds, and the log has no error lines.

scenes.name: ModernTex
scenes.line: Translates LaTeX build errors into plain explanations with a suggested fix, and marks them in the editor.
scenes.narration: If you write LaTeX on a Mac, ModernTex translates build errors into plain explanations with a suggested fix, and marks them in the editor.
